title: Rav Mesharshiya, Son of R’ Ami
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav (Hyman says it must read: of R’) Ami.

Hyman cites Kiddushin 20a for a remark found in the consulted text at [60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.60a.4), “I will explain to you the reasoning of R’ Yochanan.” The supplied text has Ami speaking, while Hyman’s print has the remark addressed to R’ Assi. Hyman suggests reversing the roles so that R’ Assi said, “I will explain to you,” since, in the print, R’ Assi was a colleague of R’ Ami. He suggests that this is the Rav Mesharshiya mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.8.4), where Rabbi Mesharshiya reports in Rabbi Idi’s name.

So too he is mentioned in [Bava Batra 85b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.85b.5), where he answers that it was a case where her husband was a seller of baskets; but this statement is in [Gittin 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.78a.8), and there it is Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Dimi.[^4]

notes.text: The supplied sentence says Ami was a colleague of Ami. It remains unresolved and is not silently changed to Assi. Hyman’s proposed reporting-role reversal and the Dimi patronymic remain separate source claims.

The whole saved Venice Rosh Hashanah4:8 scalar explicitly gives Rabbi Mesharshiya in Rabbi Idi’s name. Those exact occurrences support their full titles but do not identify this reporter as the son of Ami or Dimi. Hyman’s MUST READ Rav-to-R-prime correction does not itself specify Rabbi; the safe abbreviated title is retained there and for uninspected Yochanan/Assi/Ami occurrences. The supplied Ami was a colleague of Ami sentence is retained rather than silently corrected to Assi. His possible role reversal and apparent identification remain qualified Hyman proposals; the basket-seller answer is reported beside the distinct Gittin Dimi patronymic.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. III, p. 912) names R’ Assi as the person addressed and has “R’ Assi was a colleague of R’ Ami.” The supplied Hebrew instead gives Ami in both places. The supplied locator is Kiddushin 20a. In the corresponding passage at Kiddushin 60a, Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Ami explains Rabbi Yochanan’s reasoning to Rabbi Assi. Hyman proposes reversing those roles. Bava Batra 85b has the title Rabbi in the Ami patronymic, while Gittin 78a attributes the basket-seller answer to the son of Rav Dimi. The Venice Jerusalem Talmud passage does not give a patronymic for Rabbi Mesharshiya.

Heilprin has separate entries for [Mesharshiya son of Ami](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2572&lang=en) and [Mesharshiya son of Dimi](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2575&lang=en). The former puts Mesharshiya in the role of speaking to Assi at [Kiddushin 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.60a.4). The linked Jerusalem Talmud teaching names Rabbi Idi as the authority and gives Mesharshiya no patronymic.
